---
title: |
  Australian Household Consumption, Wealth and Credit Conditions:
  An Updated Single-Equation LIVES Estimate
author:
  - name: David Stephan
abstract: |
  We estimate the Muellbauer--Williams LIVES consumption model for
  Australia over 1988Q3--2024Q4, extending Williams (2010) and Muellbauer
  and Williams (2012) by sixteen years of post-GFC data. Wealth is
  disaggregated into housing, illiquid financial (equities plus
  superannuation) and net liquid assets (deposits net of total household
  debt), with permanent income from the local-projection forecaster of De
  Bonis, Liberati, Muellbauer and Rondinelli (2020).

  Our central finding is that the *form* of the equation is decisive. A
  conventional disaggregated error-correction model that enters wealth as
  constant-marginal-propensity levels is not the LIVES equation: in
  Williams' framework credit conditions *scale* the housing-wealth effect,
  which is zero when credit is tight. Specifying the equation faithfully
  --- housing wealth entering only through its credit-conditions
  interaction, the autonomous-consumption intercept restored, and illiquid
  financial assets combined --- yields a strongly identified
  error-correction structure: a pre-COVID speed of adjustment
  $\lambda = -0.245$ ($t = -4.8$), close to Williams' $-0.286$, with
  significant, correctly signed marginal propensities on net liquid and
  illiquid financial wealth, against an insignificant $\lambda = -0.18$
  for the constant-MPC specification.

  The LIVES *structure* transfers to Australia, but Williams' Australian
  *calibrations* do not: imposing his calibrated permanent-income gearing
  collapses the error-correction to $\lambda \approx 0$. The
  credit-conditions interactions are only weakly identified on a single
  equation because each is near-collinear with the latent index, so
  sharpening them requires the four-equation FIML system or a pre-1988
  back-extension. A CCI placebo battery, a two-equation SUR with near-zero
  residual correlation, and out-of-sample forecasts that do not beat a
  random walk are reported throughout as honest constraints on the
  single-equation approach.

keywords:
  - household consumption
  - wealth effects
  - credit conditions
  - error-correction model
  - LIVES system
jel:
  - E21
  - E32
  - E51
  - D14
